description: §8.10 Tier 2 loop hoisting (RUNTIME, sqlEngine:"real"): the hoisted loop matches each iteration's key to rows with the per-iteration query's own SQL `=`, so the key column's type affinity applies exactly as it does per row. Each cell equals the same function compiled with `.nobatch()`. Pre-fix (2dd6d35d9, S456): the pre-fetch ran `WHERE id IN (…)` (SQL matched the rows) but the loop then looked each row up in a JS Map by the key VALUE — identity, no affinity — so the text key "7" missed the INTEGER row SQL had matched (textKey "none,hello,none", numKey "0,1"), and a key the body changed before its read (`it.id = it.id + 1`) was not in the Map at all (keyChanged "none,none"). Now the pre-fetch joins a key table of (slot, key) rows, SQL tags each row with the slot of the key it matched, and the loop reads by slot; a changed key is read when its read runs.
rationale: §8.10.2: "`.get()` in the loop becomes `Map<key, Row>`; missing keys yield `not`, preserving §8.7." — a key is missing only when the per-iteration query finds no row. §8.10.3: "The rewritten loop is observationally equivalent to the un-rewritten loop on all side-effect orderings."
